title: Client contract migration map for streamed tool invocations and structured payloads
creator: Anika Bose
description: Create a prescriptive migration map and execution plan for customers and SDKs to move from legacy streaming+tool calling behavior to the new v2 API contract. The focus is streamed tool invocations (incremental partial tool payloads + final call) and changes to structured output schemas that affect client-side parsing. Deliverables: a migration checklist, SDK shim patterns, server-side dual-write mode, rollout gates, and a regression harness to validate backcompat across major client languages.
acceptance_criteria: A migration guide document published in Confluence with step-by-step instructions for self-serve customers
SDK teams (Python, Node, Java) ship shim adapters that can be toggled by customers
Server-side dual-write toggle implemented to write both old and new structured payload formats for 2 weeks in canary
Automated regression suite detects behavioral drift across streaming, function-calling, and structured outputs with a false-positive rate < 2%
Telemetry dashboards show contract errors (parse failures, schema mismatches) and are configured with alert thresholds before GA
tasks: Draft migration checklist and customer-facing FAQ
Spec: canonical mapping between old streaming fragments and v2 chunked function-call ABI
Design SDK shim API surface and backward-compatible fallback behavior
Engineering: implement dual-write on staging and a flag to route traffic to new contract in Canary
QA: author regression cases and golden prompt corpus for replay testing
Observability: add parse-error, schema-mismatch, latency-per-chunk metrics and dashboard tiles
Docs: sample migration PRs for Python/Node/Java demonstrating error handling
Solutions: prepare 3 customer outreach templates for high-risk integrations
decision_log: 2026-02-18: Agreed to use a short-lived dual-write server mode rather than on-the-wire header negotiation to minimize client churn (PM + Eng + DX)
2026-02-22: Chose incremental chunk IDs in the v2 tool-call ABI to make reordering and replay deterministic; added field 'chunk_index' and 'final_chunk' boolean
2026-02-28: Rollout cadence: internal canary (1%), public canary with opt-in flag, gradual ramp to 20% over 2 weeks, require 0 critical parse errors before GA
2026-03-05: SDK shims must expose an 'upgrade_safeguard' mode that auto-falls back on parse failures for 30s before surfacing errors to the app
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Prep: finalize spec and SDK shim API; instrument parse-error telemetry (2 weeks)
Phase 1 - Internal Canary: enable dual-write for internal teams and run replay harness (3 days)
Phase 2 - Public Opt-in Canary: release SDKs with shim; customers can opt in via header X-Redwood-API-Contract=v2 (1 week)
Phase 3 - Gradual Ramp: increase opt-in promoted traffic with feature flag manager to 20% over 14 days; monitor parse errors and latency per chunk
Phase 4 - Hard Cutover Plan: gated by <1% parse-error rate for 7 days; prepare rollback path and post-mortem template
Phase 5 - Deprecation Notice: after 30 days of stable v2, announce deprecation of legacy behavior and schedule formal removal in 90 days
test_plan: Create a golden corpus of 1,200 representative streaming prompts across conversational length, multi-tool flows, and adversarial inputs
Automated replay harness that can inject recorded traffic into staging with both old and new contract parsers and compare outputs token-by-token
Mutation tests that flip chunk order, drop intermediate chunks, and inject duplicate chunks to validate chunk resilience
Integration tests for SDK shims in Python/Node/Java that simulate parse failures and exercise fallback logic
Load test dual-write path at 5x expected production QPS to ensure no perf regression
Chaos test: flip dual-write off/on during in-flight streams to validate client idempotency and server reconcilers
Define a small set of canary assertions (no critical parse errors, <5% increase in 95th latency per request, no increase in function-call misfires)
